{{Current events|year=2019|month=11|day=24|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)]]
**[[Taliban]] [[insurgent]]s storm a [[security checkpoint|checkpoint]] in [[Daykundi Province]], killing eight [[Afghan Army]] personnel. After reinforcements were sent to the area, Afghan soldiers drive off the attackers, killing at least 20 of them. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/asia_pacific/afghan-official-taliban-storm-army-checkpoint-killing-8/2019/11/24/838196c0-0eb3-11ea-924c-b34d09bbc948_story.html (Washington Post)]
**A [[Grenade|grenade]] attack in [[Kabul]] hit an [[United Nations]] car killing one foreigner and injuring five others. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-blast/grenade-thrown-at-u-n-vehicle-in-kabul-one-foreigner-killed-idUSKBN1XY0I2 (Reuters)]
*[[2019 Iraqi protests]]
**Security forces opened fire on protesters, killing nine and wounding dozens. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iraq-protests/security-forces-kill-nine-in-iraq-protests-idUSKBN1XY04Z (Reuters)]
*[[2019 Lebanese protests]]
**Clashes between anti-government protestors, and [[Hezbollah]] and [[Amal Movement]] supporters break out when the former group blocked a main bridge in downtown [[Beirut]]. At least five people are injured. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-lebanon-protests/lebanese-protesters-clash-with-supporters-of-hezbollah-amal-in-downtown-beirut-idUSKBN1XZ013?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2019 Busy Bee crash]]
**A [[plane crash]]es shortly after [[takeoff]] in a densely populated neighborhood of the city of [[Goma]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], killing all the 19 people on board. About ten other people are killed on the ground. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-congo-crash/plane-crash-kills-at-least-18-in-eastern-congo-idUSKBN1XY06H (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-50536220 (BBC)]

;International relations
*[[Foreign relations of Tuvalu]]
**Tuvaluan Foreign Minister [[Simon Kofe]] says Tuvalu rejects Chinese offers to build artificial islands for his country, which deals with rising sea levels because Tuvalu sees the offers as an "attempt to reduce [[Taiwanese]] influence in the Pacific region". Tuvalu is one of four Pacific nations to recognize Taiwan in the [[One-China policy]] dispute. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/403936/tuvalu-s-artificial-islands-won-t-be-made-in-china (RNZ)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Bolivian political crisis]]
**[[Bolivia]]'s [[Plurinational Legislative Assembly|legislative assembly]] approves the annulment of the [[2019 Bolivian general election|October general election]] and the holding of new elections. Ex-[[President of Bolivia|president]] [[Evo Morales]] is barred from participating. [https://www.dw.com/en/bolivia-approves-new-elections-excluding-evo-morales/a-51387746 (DW)] 
*[[2019 Guinea-Bissau presidential election]]
**Citizens of [[Guinea-Bissau]] head to the polls to vote for a new [[List of presidents of Guinea-Bissau|president]] amidst political turmoil. [https://www.euronews.com/2019/11/24/guinea-bissau-votes-for-president-after-weeks-of-political-upset (Euronews)]
*[[2019 Hong Kong protests]], [[2019 Hong Kong local elections]]
**[[Elections in Hong Kong|Local elections]] are held in [[Hong Kong]]. Barring military intervention from Beijing, the outcome is seen as a major indicator for the political future of the protest-ridden region. [https://www.dw.com/en/hong-kong-record-turnout-for-district-elections/a-51387049 (DW)]
**With a record 71% turnout, the [[Pro-democracy camp (Hong Kong)|pro-democracy camp]] wins 333 of 452 seats up for election. [[Jimmy Sham]], one of the leaders of the protest, won in his electorate while major [[Pro-Beijing camp (Hong Kong)|pro-Beijing]] leader [[Junius Ho]] lost in his. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-protests/hong-kong-democrats-romp-to-local-election-landslide-after-months-of-protests-idUSKBN1XY0MZ (Reuters)] 
*[[2019 Romanian presidential election]]
**People of [[Romania]] cast their vote in the second round of the latest presidential election. [https://www.dw.com/en/romania-seeking-a-return-to-normality/a-51380802 (DW)]
*[[2019 Uruguayan general election]]
**[[Uruguay]] holds the second round of the 2019 presidential election. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/11/ruling-party-faces-exit-uruguay-votes-president-191124081851651.html (Aljazeera)]
*[[2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries]], [[Michael Bloomberg 2020 presidential campaign]]
**Former [[Mayor of New York City]] [[Michael Bloomberg]] announces he's running for the presidency as part of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] ticket. [https://www.npr.org/2019/11/24/782096579/former-new-york-mayor-michael-bloomberg-is-running-for-president (NPR)]
*[[United States Secretary of Defense|U.S. Secretary of Defense]] [[Mark Esper]] forces [[United States Secretary of the Navy|Navy Secretary]] [[Richard V. Spencer]] to resign over his handling of the court martial of [[United States Navy SEALs|Navy SEAL]] [[Eddie Gallagher (Navy SEAL)|Eddie Gallagher]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-military-seals/u-s-defense-secretary-fires-navy-chief-over-handling-of-seal-saga-idUSKBN1XY0M5 (Reuters)]

;Sports
*[[2019 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]]
**With four rounds to go, [[Clube de Regatas do Flamengo|Flamengo]] wins the [[Football in Brazil|Brazilian]] league for the sixth time. They are the first team since 1963's [[Santos FC]] to win the national league and the [[Copa Libertadores]] on the same weekend. [https://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/flamengo/noticia/flamengo-e-campeao-brasileiro-e-se-torna-primeiro-time-desde-1963-a-ganhar-nacional-e-libertadores-no-mesmo-ano.ghtml (Globo Esporte)]
*[[2019 CFL season]]
**The [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] win the [[107th Grey Cup]], defeating the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] 33-12, in Winnipeg's first [[Grey Cup]] win since 1990. Winnipeg running back [[Andrew Harris (Canadian football)|Andrew Harris]] becomes the first player in Grey Cup history to be named both [[Grey Cup Most Valuable Player|Most Valuable Player]] and [[Dick Suderman Trophy|Most Valuable Canadian]]. [https://www.sportsnet.ca/football/cfl/blue-bombers-andrew-harris-becomes-first-win-grey-cup-mop-moc/ (Sportsnet)]
